title: Ordinary resolution to increase share capital
ruleSource: Written from S.A Badmus' Corporate Law drafts (Lawdeck knowledge base). To be confirmed by the legal reviewer, including every section of the Companies and Allied Matters Act 2020 cited.

parts.why: Company documents carry the company's name, registered address and registration (RC) number, and for resolutions and notices the statutory heading. Source: Corporate Law Practice drafting materials (Lawdeck knowledge base).

parts.text: ORDINARY RESOLUTION TO INCREASE THE SHARE CAPITAL OF THE COMPANY PURSUANT TO SECTION 127 OF THE COMPANIES AND ALLIED MATTERS ACT 2020
parts.why: The title and the law relied on. Source: Corporate Law Practice drafting materials (Lawdeck knowledge base).

parts.text:
At the general meeting of the company held on {{meetingDate}} at {{meetingPlace}}, the following resolution was proposed and duly passed:

"That the share capital of the company be increased from {{currentCapital}} to {{newCapital}} by the creation of {{newShares}} additional ordinary shares of {{shareValue}} each, such new shares ranking pari passu in all respects with the existing shares of the company."
parts.why: The resolution: the present and new capital, the shares created and their value, and that they rank pari passu with existing shares. Source: Corporate Law Practice drafting materials (Lawdeck knowledge base).

Resolutions are dated and signed, usually by two directors or a director and the secretary. Always sign and date in the exam, on or before the exam date. Source: Corporate Law Practice drafting materials (Lawdeck knowledge base).
